newsitem.title: UK: IRA calls new truce to get Sinn Fein to talks.
newsitem.headline: IRA calls new truce to get Sinn Fein to talks.

text.p: The IRA on Saturday announced a new ceasefire in its 28-year guerrilla war against British rule of Northern Ireland, to take effect at noon on Sunday.
The announcement was made in a statement to Ireland's state RTE broadcasting network in Dublin, which the guerrillas see as the capital of a reunited Ireland.

The ceasefire, which restores a truce the guerrillas called in August 1994 and broke in February 1996, will allow its Sinn Fein political wing to claim a seat at Northern Ireland peace talks within six weeks.
The statement said that "all IRA units have been instructed accordingly" and would be stood down.
It said it was an "an unequivocal restoration of the ceasefire of August 1994".
Britain had demanded that the guerrillas call an unconditional truce to gain a seat at the talks between pro-Irish nationalists and pro-British Unionists.
It was the first time the guerrillas had used the word "unequivocal" in any recent statement.

The ceasefire was signalled on Friday when Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams said he would urge the guerrillas to call a new truce so that his party could take part in year-old talks from which it has been barred because of the IRA's war.
The key to the new truce was British reassurances that Sinn Fein could claim a seat at the talks without having first to get the IRA to surrender the arms it has used in its war.
Instead, the issue of "decommissioning" will be discussed in parallel with political negotiations on a settlement to a conflict that has killed 3,200 in 28 years.
